title: The determinant and inverse conjecture for E0_2-matrices
statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be an $\mathbf{E_{0_2}}$-matrix.

**Determinant and inverse conjecture.** One has

$$
\det(A)<0,
$$

$A^{-1}$ exists, and $A^{-1}$ is a $\mathbf{Z}$-matrix.

This is one of the conjectures proposed after examples and observations about $\mathbf{E_{0_2}}$-matrices. The supplied text gives no evidence of a proof or refutation, so its resolution remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).
source_name: Bharat Pratap Chauhan and Dipti Dubey, “On semimonotone matrices of exact order two”, arXiv:2603.00639 (2026).
